name: Kepler / K2
full_name: Kepler Space Telescope dark matter microlensing analyses
summary: Space photometry mission primarily designed for exoplanets. Its public light curves have been used in dedicated analyses searching for primordial-black-hole dark matter.
detection_principle: Searches stellar light curves for short, approximately symmetric gravitational-lensing brightenings, simulates detection efficiency and constrains the primordial-black-hole fraction.

timeline.event: Launch, using the local date on NASA's page
Second reaction wheel failed, ending the original mission; subsequently repurposed as K2

collaboration.name: Kepler / K2 collaboration / mission team
collaboration.participants_note: Only examples of lead or participating institutions directly established by the sources are listed. This is not a complete collaboration list, and listing does not imply equal institutional roles.

key_parameters.name: Primary-mirror diameter
key_parameters.value: About 1.4 m; the entrance aperture is about 1 m, a different quantity

phases.name: Original Kepler mission
phases.description: Long-term high-precision photometry of a fixed sky field

phases.name: K2
phases.description: Extended mission stabilized using solar-radiation pressure after reaction-wheel failure

results.summary: Two years of light curves were searched for primordial-black-hole lensing, producing mass-dependent upper limits.

science_scope: Constrains dark-matter distribution and properties through gravity, microlensing or structure statistics; does not directly identify dark-matter particles.
